newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr runs into heavy selling, ends 1/2 cent down.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr runs into heavy selling, ends 1/2 cent down.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ran into heavy selling on Wednesday, closing nearly half a U.S. cent lower after comments from Finance Minister Bill Birch and Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash.
The comments coincided with a big sell order and key support levels were smashed. Dealers said the kiwi had found new support at US$0.6880-90 and they expect a partial bounce.
Any rebound however, could be conditional on the big sell order being filled and on long-term U.S. holders of kiwi not taking fright and bailing out, dealers said.
At 5.00 p.m. (0500 GMT) the kiwi was at US$0.6893/00, slightly above its 0.6884 low, after it had opened at 0.6944/51.
The Trade-Weighted Index also ended sharply lower, at 67.88 from 68.32 at the opening.
Brash helped send the kiwi down when he repeated earlier comments that the currency was overvalued.
Shortly later, Birch told Reuters that the factors behind the kiwi's rapid rise were no longer present and that added to the bearishness.
"We've run into solid buying at 0.6880 and I think there is room for a bounce to 0.6930," said one dealer.
She was sceptical of Brash's comments. "How many times have we been told that? I think the kiwi is finding a bit of a bottom and I think we will rally from here."
